reason: Chapter 24 'Chloromethanes and Tetrachloroethylene' of the cited `2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf` is this dataset's chapter. Its two inventory tables, Tab. 24.2 (p.301) and Tab. 24.3 (p.302), are captioned 'In- / Outputs for the modules "methyl chloride, at plant", "dichloromethane, at plant", "trichloroethylene, at plant" ...' but they hold the cumulated Boustead vectors of those datasets - resources, emissions and waste-treatment services, no production input - i.e. the targets' own answers, which the ecoSpold comment of this dataset states as well ('The data source for this process is a system inventory from Boustead. Due to the cumulated form of this data only the ressources and emissions included in the data source were considered'). For methyl chloride the chapter shows two different routes in Fig. 24.4 (methane chlorination) and Fig. 24.5 (methanol hydrochlorination) and then states, sec. 24.5.2: 'There was no information in those cumulated inventory data about the share of the two processes considered. Also the used allocation method to share the burdens between the obtained products in the methane chlorination process (methyl chloride, dichloromethane, chloroform, carbon tetrachloride) was unclear.' The dataset's own ecoSpold technology field says the same: 'Data refers to actual technology used in the companies included. This leads in total to an average value including all important production routes for this chemical.' Route share unknown and co-product allocation unknown. Per the rule that the cited report is not the only report that may document a dataset, all 114 bundled reports were converted with pdftotext and searched for an inventory of this dataset. No other bundled report models chloromethane production.
